title: Kumble Wants Kuldeep. Pathan Wants Washington. India's Test XI for Afghanistan Has Two Spots Still in Play.
excerpt: The one-off Test at Mullanpur starts June 6. Gill will captain for the first time. The bowling combination remains the only question.
body:
India and Afghanistan will meet in a one-off Test at the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium in Mullanpur from June 6. It is India's first Test since sharing the Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy with England — five draws in five matches — and Afghanistan's return to Indian soil for red-ball cricket eight years after the two countries first played a Test.

Shubman Gill will lead India in Tests for the first time. KL Rahul has been named vice-captain. The regular leadership group — Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli — are absent from the Test squad, resting ahead of the ODI series that follows. Neither is Jasprit Bumrah, whose workload has been carefully managed since the Australia tour.

## The Squad

India's 15-man squad has a clear shape. Gill, Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Sai Sudharsan, and Devdutt Padikkal form the batting core. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel are the wicketkeeping options. Nitish Kumar Reddy adds the all-rounder dimension at No. 7. Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna lead the pace attack. Gurnoor Brar, the left-arm seamer from Punjab who impressed in IPL 2026 with Gujarat Titans, is in line for a debut.

The complication — and where former captains are beginning to disagree publicly — is the spin composition.

## The Kumble-Pathan Split

On the Star Sports show *Follow the Blues*, Anil Kumble named his preferred XI. He picked Kuldeep Yadav and Harsh Dubey as his two frontline spinners, alongside Siraj and Brar as the pace pair. The logic is straightforward: Kuldeep took eight wickets at 28.63 in the last home Test series against South Africa. Dubey, who earned his maiden call-up through consistent Ranji Trophy performances, would be the containing off-spin option.

Irfan Pathan disagreed on exactly one spot. He replaced Kuldeep with Washington Sundar.

"The Indian team likes to bat till No. 8," Pathan explained. "So maybe in place of Kuldeep Yadav, at No. 6, No. 7, and No. 8 — Dhruv Jurel, Nitish Kumar Reddy, and Washington Sundar."

The argument is not about quality. Kuldeep is the more dangerous wicket-taker; Washington offers batting insurance. In Mullanpur's June heat — temperatures have been touching 43 degrees — the pitch will likely turn from Day 2 onwards, making the spin combination more consequential than it might appear against Afghanistan.

## Net Bowlers and the Auqib Nabi Story

Seven additional players have been called as net bowlers to assist India's preparations. Among them is Auqib Nabi, the Jammu and Kashmir left-arm seamer who finished as the highest wicket-taker in Ranji Trophy 2025-26 and guided his state to a maiden title. Prince Yadav, earmarked for the ODI squad, is also in Mullanpur already.

A BCCI source told PTI that the decision was driven by the extreme weather. "Due to extreme weather conditions, the two premier fast bowlers, Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna, can't go flat out in the nets after a gruelling three games in seven days with travel. The batters would need adequate practice."

## Gill's Challenge

The transition from IPL to Test cricket is always compressed, but this year's turnaround is historically tight. Gill played four Delhi Capitals matches in the final week of IPL 2026 before reporting to Mullanpur. He has never led India in a Test. His task against Afghanistan is partly about building a case for more permanent leadership — the BCCI is watching how he handles an inexperienced squad, a flat pitch, and the pressure of captaincy.

Inside Sport India reported that while most squad members have arrived in Mullanpur, Gill himself was not yet seen at the team hotel as of June 2. His arrival is expected imminently.

## Hardik Pandya's Fitness Question

While the Test is Gill's concern, the ODI series that follows carries its own intrigue. Hardik Pandya has been named in the ODI squad subject to fitness clearance. He is scheduled to report to the BCCI Centre of Excellence to undergo tests. Reports indicate he bowled at 135.7 kmph and lifted 120 kg weights at the CoE to reduce body fat. If he is cleared, the ODI squad gains an elite all-rounder for the three matches against Afghanistan in Dharamsala, Lucknow, and Chennai.

There is no clarity yet on whether Rohit Sharma, also listed subject to fitness, will be available for the ODI series.

## The NRI Angle

For Indian cricket fans abroad, the Afghanistan series is the start of a packed summer. The Test is followed by three ODIs (June 13-20), then two T20Is in Ireland (June 26-28), and a full tour of England starting July 1 — five T20Is and three ODIs. Zee Sports and SonyLIV will carry the India-Afghanistan matches. The England tour, with its UK-friendly time zones, will be the most accessible live cricket for NRIs since the 2024 Ashes.

## What to Watch

The Afghanistan Test is unlikely to be a contest of equals — India have never lost to Afghanistan in any format — but it is a consequential match for careers. Padikkal, Brar, and Dubey are all pushing for places in the longer-term Test XI. Jurel will want to stake his claim against Pant. And Gill, for all his talent with the bat, faces the entirely different challenge of directing a bowling attack in conditions that will test patience as much as skill.

The Test begins Saturday, June 6. First ball is at 9:30 AM IST.
